title: The Hidden Code Behind the FTX Collapse: "Allow Negative"

lines.say: FTX told customers their deposits were theirs. Its terms of service said customer assets could not be loaned to FTX.

scene.q: none of the digital assets in [a customer's] account are the property of, or shall or may be loaned to, FTX Trading.
scene.cite: As quoted in the gov't sentencing memorandum

lines.say: But according to trial evidence cited by prosecutors, special features were written into FTX's code for Sam Bankman-Fried's trading firm, Alameda Research.
One was called allow negative. Alameda's balance could go below zero.
lines.show: One was called "allow negative." Alameda's balance could go below zero.

lines.say: Another was a sixty-five billion dollar line of credit. And Alameda was exempt from automatic liquidation.
lines.show: Another was a $65 billion line of credit. And Alameda was exempt from automatic liquidation.

lines.say: By June two thousand twenty-two, according to trial evidence, a spreadsheet showed Alameda borrowing thirteen billion dollars in customer funds.
lines.show: By June 2022, according to trial evidence, a spreadsheet showed Alameda borrowing $13 billion in customer funds.

scene.label: in FTX customer funds|borrowed by Alameda

lines.say: In twenty twenty-three, a jury convicted Bankman-Fried on all seven counts, including fraud.
lines.show: In 2023, a jury convicted Bankman-Fried on all 7 counts, including fraud.
